The Imagery Data Manager (IDM) platform was developed for the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement (OSMRE) to automate imagery management and processing workflows. OSMRE wanted to enable uploading to compliant storage from low bandwidth environments, optimize routine processing workflows, and enable data sharing. Prior to IDM, the effort to ingest, archive, process and share numerous types of UAV based data was labor intensive. Since OSMRE operates in many remote locations with unreliable access to the internet and limited bandwidth, uploading and managing remote sensing outputs to the cloud was not practical. Large amounts of data ended up siloed on multiple laptops, resulting in imagery not being used due to the inability to find them across the organization.

Administration of the IDM system must be done by users with the Administrator role. Administrators can do all the functions of a Field Worker (see the Field Worker Guides) but also have the ability to administer the configuration of the IDM system.
The Manage Accounts section of the System Configuration page lists all users in IDM. Use it to add, bulk upload, export, edit, disable, and delete users.
Custom hierarchies are synchronized from an instance of GeoPrism Registry. When imported to IDM they enable the ability to filter the map data in the Site Viewer by the geographies that are imported.

The email settings allow administrators to configure the connection properties for the email server used by IDM. To open them, choose System Configuration from the navigation menu, and click Configure Email in the System Email section. All fields are required. Emails are sent to users of the system to notify of important events. For example, an email is sent to a Field Worker once an upload has successfully finished.

Administrators can write a help page for each organization. When users click Need some help? in the IDM header, they see the help page for their organization. This should be the first place users go for support, so use it to tell them how to reach your organization's help desk. See Getting Help for what users see.
The Manage System Images section of the System Configuration page allows administrators to configure the images used for the logo in the header of IDM.
Organizations are pulled from SAM.gov into an instance of GeoPrism Registry that’s managed for IDM. IDM then pulls those from GeoPrism Registry through a formal synchronization widget in IDM.

IDM hosts all published image mosaic and elevation products in the public SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog (STAC), Know-STAC, making these products available as Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs (COG). This means that all published COGs are available from standard COG API functionality. See Cloud Native Formats for why IDM uses COGs.

Data Upload

Field Workers are the primary users of IDM. Their primary tasks are to upload data, process data into products, share products, and create metadata. These guides provide instructions on how to complete different tasks and workflows in the application.
There are multiple places that files can be downloaded depending on what you’re viewing in IDM and what needs to be downloaded.

Image sets are groupings of raw images from the raw tab of a collection that are created to share sets of raw images. They make it easier to highlight selections of raw images that show something of interest. Some example uses are to share a couple raw images that have issues or highlight something in the field that stands out in the imagery.

A collection is where the primary data is organized and operations on that data are made. Raw data is uploaded to a collection and products are generated from it. See Data Hierarchy for how collections fit with sites, projects, and missions.
There can be one or more missions within a project. A mission defines a tactical field operation to collect data in a specific area, for a specific purpose, and within a specific time range.
A private collection is hidden from other IDM users. Only these users can see it:
There can be one or more projects within a site. A project defines the operational project that all work is conducted for.
A site is the top most level of the data hierarchy and includes the location of where the data is collected.
Products are stand-alone assets made up of harmonized imagery, elevation, or LiDAR data. Products in IDM are created from one of two methods.

The collection modal is where all raw images that have been uploaded to a collection (in one or multiple uploads) and the most recently processed output products are stored. All products derived using IDM functionality are configured in the collection modal or the processing workflow and built from the data in the raw tab.

Many sensors contain embedded georeference information in their EXIF headers which are used for aligning raw images into mosaics. If this information does not exist in the EXIF headers a geologger file can be used (e.g. RX1R2 sensors).

Ground control points are useful for correcting distortions in the data and referencing the data to known coordinate systems. A Ground Control Point (GCP) is a position measurement made on the ground, typically using a high precision GPS. (Toffanin 2019)

Products created or refined using external tools can be uploaded to the products tab of a collection for storage. Products can also be uploaded to a project or mission without a collection, when you have products but no raw data to store in IDM.
Products can be viewed from the products tab of a collection or from the Products tab of the Site Viewer sidebar.

Products can be shared publicly by publishing a specific product. The publish functionality registers the product on the public IDM Know-STAC and makes a variety of methods for accessing the data available to anyone outside of IDM.

The Raw directory (RAW tab) of a Collection is where unprocessed or minimally processed data from a flight is stored. Uploading to the Raw directory ensures that your data is stored on the government cloud in a compliant manner and makes the data available for generating derived products.
LiDAR can be uploaded to the raw directory of collections for storage as well as for further processing into derived products.
Multispectral imagery can be uploaded to the raw directory of collections for storage as well as for further processing into derived products.
Still imagery (RGB) can be uploaded to the raw directory of collections for storage as well as for further processing into derived products.
Videos can be uploaded to the raw directory of collections for storage as well as for further processing into derived products.

The Imagery Data Manager (IDM) platform was developed for the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement (OSMRE) to automate imagery management and processing workflows. OSMRE wanted to enable uploading to compliant storage from low bandwidth environments, optimize routine processing workflows, and enable data sharing. Prior to IDM, the effort to ingest, archive, process and share numerous types of UAV based data was labor intensive. Since OSMRE operates in many remote locations with unreliable access to the internet and limited bandwidth, uploading and managing remote sensing outputs to the cloud was not practical. Large amounts of data ended up siloed on multiple laptops, resulting in imagery not being used due to the inability to find them across the organization. The IDM platform solves these problems by providing a cloud-based solution that streamlines the upload, metadata capture, management, and processing workflows of data obtained by remote sensors. Large amounts of data can be uploaded even when the internet is poor and unreliable. It also automates the ingest process, data delivery, and capture of an expanded version of the standard specifications for metadata and data formats required by the USGS EROS Center. The IDM was designed with extensibility in mind. Since it is built entirely out of open source components, common functionality can be shared across organizations. This will result in cost savings and productivity gains as it is adopted by additional organizations and agencies. While OSMRE originally funded IDM, it is now managed by the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) and hosted as a Department of the Interior (DOI) project on GeoPlatform.

Administration of the IDM system must be done by users with the Administrator role. Administrators can do all the functions of a Field Worker (see the Field Worker Guides) but also have the ability to administer the configuration of the IDM system. Administration pages are opened from the navigation menu in the upper right hand corner of IDM. Administrators see four extra items at the bottom of the menu: UAV, Equipment, System Configuration and System Info.
UAV Registration: register the UAVs used to collect data.
Platforms and Sensors: register the platforms and sensors used to collect data, and the types, manufacturers and wave lengths they are built from.

The System Configuration page has a section for each of these, from top to bottom: Accounts (Manage Accounts): add, bulk upload, and edit users and their roles. Icons (Manage System Images): change the IDM logo. Email Settings (System Email): configure the email server used for notifications. Session Event Log: monitor user sign-ins. Organizations (Organizations and Organization Integrations): synchronize the organizations users and data belong to. Custom Hierarchies (GeoPrism Registry Integrations): import geographic hierarchies for filtering sites in the Site Viewer.
System Info: see the IDM and Open Drone Map versions that are running, and the release notes.

Help Pages: write the organization-specific help pages users see when they click Need some help?. Reporting: collection and processing quality reports, from the Report menu item. The collection report is available to all users; the processing quality report is only available to Administrators. Public Image Services: access published products as Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs.
The Manage Accounts section of the System Configuration page lists all users in IDM. Use it to add, bulk upload, export, edit, disable, and delete users.

Sign in as an Administrator. Open the navigation menu in the upper right hand corner of IDM and choose System Configuration. Manage Accounts is the first section of the page. The users table has the columns Username, First name, Last name, Phone Number, Email Address, and Organization. Type in the box under a column header to filter the table. Use the page numbers under the table to see more users. On deployments that use single sign-on, users added in IDM have their email address as their username. Their first name, last name, and phone number come from the single sign-on system and are updated each time they sign in, so these columns are blank until the user signs in for the first time.

Role Description Administrator Administrators can do all the functions of a Field Worker but also have the ability to administer the configuration of the IDM system. Field Worker Field Workers are the primary users of IDM. Their primary tasks are to upload data, process data into products, and create metadata. See the Field Worker Guides for more details. Roles are set with the checkboxes in the System roles section of the add and edit forms. A user can have more than one role. New users have the Field Worker role checked by default.

On deployments that use single sign-on, a person can only sign in to IDM after an administrator has added them here. IDM matches the email address of the person signing in to the email address of a user in IDM. Click the Add new User button under the users table. Fill out the fields and click Submit. Field Description Email Address Required. This MUST match the email address the person uses in the single sign-on system. It can't be the same as the email address of another user. Organization The organization the user is a part of. This field can be left blank. Extra Information Any additional information about the user and their involvement in tasks or data related to IDM. System roles One checkbox for each role. Field Worker is checked by default.

These options are only available on deployments that don't require single sign-on. The Add new User form also has the fields First name, Last name, Phone Number, Username, Password, and Confirm password. First name, last name, email address, username, and password are required. The password must be at least 14 characters long and contain at least two uppercase letters, two lowercase letters, two digits, and two special characters. Instead of entering a user's details yourself, you can invite them by email: Click the Invite User button above the users table. In the Invite a User form, enter the Email Address, choose an Organization, check the System roles, and click Submit. IDM emails the person a link to finish creating their account. On that page they enter their name, phone number, email address, username, and password. The link stops working after a set number of hours, which the email states. Invitations are sent with the server set up in Email Settings.

Click the Export Users button under the users table to download a list of all users. The download is a zip file, idm-users.zip, containing one CSV file (currently named session-event-export.csv). It has one row per user and these columns: Column Description username The user's username. firstName First name. lastName Last name. organization The name of the user's organization. email Email address. phoneNumber Phone number. oid The user's internal IDM identifier. The export lists organization names, not the organization codes that Bulk Uploading Users expects, so it can't be uploaded again as is.

Users can be uploaded in bulk with a spreadsheet. Each new user is assigned the organization and role set in the spreadsheet. If the spreadsheet has no Role column, every new user is assigned the Field Worker role. Spreadsheet Requirements The spreadsheet must be in CSV format. There must be a header row containing column names. The required columns are First Name, Last Name, Email, and Organization. Role is optional. Column names are not case sensitive and spaces are ignored, but they must otherwise match the names in the table below. For example, First Name and firstname both work, but Email Address is not recognized. Columns with other names are ignored. Click on the Upload Users button to open the upload users modal. Drag and drop a .CSV file containing the users to add, or click to select one. The upload starts as soon as the file is selected. Column Required Description First Name Yes First name of the user being added. Last Name Yes Last name of the user being added. Email Yes Email address of the user being added. This MUST match the email being used in the single sign on system that IDM is integrated with. Organization (or Org) Yes Organization that the user being added is a part of. This MUST be set to the code of an organization registered in the IDM system. You can find this code in the Organizations section of the administration pages of IDM. Role No Set to admin to make the user an Administrator. Warning: if the spreadsheet has a Role column, any user whose value is not admin, including a blank value, is created with no role. Leave the Role column out entirely to make every user a Field Worker, or set roles afterwards by editing each user. warning Users whose email address already exists in IDM are skipped. Their accounts aren't changed. Email addresses are not case sensitive. The upload is all or nothing. If any row has an error, such as an organization code that doesn't exist, no users are added. The error message gives the line number of the problem row. Fix it and upload the whole file again.

Editing a user allows you to change the fields that are managed by IDM. On deployments that use single sign-on, the fields that come from the single sign-on system are shown in grey and can't be edited. Find the user in the users table in the Manage Accounts section. Click the edit button (pencil) on the far right of the row to open the user form. Change the fields and click Submit. Field Description First name First name of the user. On single sign-on deployments it comes from the single sign-on system and can't be edited. Last name Last name of the user. On single sign-on deployments it comes from the single sign-on system and can't be edited. Phone Number Phone number of the user. On single sign-on deployments it comes from the single sign-on system and can't be edited. Email Address Email address of the user. On single sign-on deployments this is how IDM recognizes the user when they sign in, so it MUST match the email address they use in the single sign-on system. Organization Organization that the user is a part of. This field can be left blank if no applicable organization exists in the list. Extra Information Any additional information about the user and their involvement in tasks or data related to IDM. Username Only on deployments that don't require single sign-on. The username of the admin user can't be changed. Change password? Only on deployments that don't require single sign-on. Check it to show the Password and Confirm password fields and set a new password. Disabled Check it to deactivate the user. A disabled user can't sign in. It is not shown for the admin user. System roles One checkbox for each role. Check every role the user should have.
To stop a user from signing in without removing them from IDM, edit the user, check Disabled, and click Submit. Uncheck it to let them sign in again. The admin user can't be disabled.

Find the user in the users table in the Manage Accounts section. Click the delete button (trash can) on the far right of the row. Click Delete to confirm. Deleting a user can't be undone. To keep the user's record, deactivate them instead. The admin user can't be deleted.

documents.t: info Synchronization profiles must connect to an instance of GeoPrism Registry that contains a hierarchy of geographies you would like to import to IDM. From the System Configuration page, scroll down to the GeoPrism Registry Integrations section. Click the Add new Synchronization Profile button to open the screen for creating a new profile. Enter the URL of an instance of GeoPrism Registry containing the geographic hierarchy you’d like to import. IDM connects to that instance when you leave the URL field (for example, by pressing Tab or clicking elsewhere). The URL must start with http:// or https://. If IDM can't reach the server, an error message is shown. If successfully connected, the Remote Labeled Property Graph Type field appears. Select the graph containing the data to import. After selecting the type, the Remote Labeled Property Graph Entry field appears. Select the date of the graph. After selecting the entry, the Remote Labeled Property Graph Version field appears. Select the version of the graph. Push the Apply button. Apply stays disabled until all fields are filled out. After a profile is created, its fields are read-only. To use a different server or graph, delete the profile and create a new one. To move to a newer version of the same graph, use Check for new version (see below).

Open an existing synchronization profile by clicking its eye icon. Push the Synchronize from server button. A progress indicator is shown while the synchronization runs. The profile screen also has these buttons: Check for new version: checks the GeoPrism Registry server for a newer version of the same graph entry. If one is found, IDM asks whether to upgrade to it. Pushing Upgrade switches the profile to the newest version and synchronizes it from the server. This action can't be undone. If there is no newer version, IDM shows "No newer versions were found." Create tiles: generates the map tiles for the synchronized geographies.

Administrators can write a help page for each organization. When users click Need some help? in the IDM header, they see the help page for their organization. This should be the first place users go for support, so use it to tell them how to reach your organization's help desk. See Getting Help for what users see.

Users see the help page for the organization assigned to their account. If that organization doesn't have a help page, IDM shows the page of a higher-level organization in the organization hierarchy. A help page written for a parent organization therefore acts as the default for all organizations below it that don't have their own.

Click Need some help? in the header at the top of any IDM page. The help page opens in a new browser tab. Select the organization whose help page you want to edit in the organization field at the top of the page. Start typing to search, or click the tree picker (three dots) to browse the full organization tree and select a specific organization. Click the edit (pencil) button. If the organization doesn't have a help page yet, the editor opens with a template you can fill in. Write the page in Markdown in the editor. A preview of the page is shown next to the editor as you type. Click Save to publish the page, or Cancel to discard your changes.

The template has sections for: your organization's help desk contacts: portal URL, email, phone, support hours and preferred contact method instructions on which contact method to use templates users can copy for bug reports, feature requests and general questions organization-specific documentation and training resources other notes, such as policies or escalation guidance Replace the placeholder text in brackets with your organization's details, and remove any sections you don't need. tip Tell users when to escalate to the IDM help desk at support@terraframe.com, which provides general IDM support when organization support isn't adequate. Platforms and sensors are managed on the Equipment page. Open it by choosing Equipment from the navigation menu. Only Administrators can see this menu item. The page has four sections, from top to bottom: Sensor Options: the lists of Sensor Types and Wave Lengths that sensors are built from. Sensors: the table of registered sensors. Platform Options: the lists of Platform Types and Platform Manufacturers that platforms are built from. Platforms: the table of registered platforms. A platform must have at least one sensor, so register sensors before the platforms that carry them.

The Sensor Options and Platform Options sections hold the lists of values offered in the sensor and platform forms: List Used for Sensor Types The Type field on a sensor (for example, Multispectral). Wave Lengths The Wave Length checkboxes on a sensor. Platform Types The Type field on a platform (for example, fixed wing). Platform Manufacturer The Manufacturer field on a platform. Click a list's heading to expand or collapse it. Each list is a table of names: To add a value, click the Add new … button below the table, enter a Name, and click Apply. To view or edit a value, click the view icon in its row. Click Edit, change the name, and click Apply. To remove a value, click the remove icon in its row and confirm. A sensor type, platform type or platform manufacturer can't be removed while a sensor or platform uses it.
The Sensors table lists every registered sensor with its Name, Model, Description and Type.

On the Equipment page, click Add new Sensor below the Sensors table. Fill out the sensor form. Click Apply. To change a sensor, click the view icon in its row, then click Edit. To remove a sensor, click the remove icon in its row and confirm.

Field Required Description Name Yes Name of the sensor (example: Anafi). Description No Description of the sensor. Model Yes Model of the sensor (example: Micasense Altum (w/o thermal) 2064x1544 (R,G,B,RE, NIR) 7.1 [mm] x 5.3 [mm] FL 8). Type Yes Type of sensor, chosen from the Sensor Types list (example: Multispectral). Formats Captured With This Sensor At least one The kinds of data this sensor captures. When a Field Worker creates a collection with this sensor, only these formats are offered as the collection's format. A new sensor starts with Still Imagery, Still thermal imagery (non-radiometric), Video and Thermal video (non-radiometric) checked; uncheck any the sensor doesn't capture. The options are: - Still Imagery - Still thermal imagery (non-radiometric) - Still thermal imagery (radiometric) - Multispectral Still Imagery - Video - Thermal video (non-radiometric) - Thermal video (radiometric) - Multispectral Video - LIDAR Has GeoLogger No Check this if the sensor writes image locations to a separate geo location (geologger) file instead of the images' EXIF headers. Collections using this sensor must have a geo location file uploaded before they can be processed. High Resolution No Check this for high resolution sensors. When processing a collection that uses this sensor, IDM defaults to a finer resolution (2 cm instead of 5 cm) and higher point cloud quality. Pixel Size Width Yes Pixel size width of the sensor. Recorded in collection metadata. Pixel Size Height Yes Pixel size height of the sensor. Recorded in collection metadata. Sensor Width Yes Width of the sensor, in millimeters. Sensor Height Yes Height of the sensor, in millimeters. Focal Length Yes Focal length of the sensor, in millimeters. Wave Length At least one The wave lengths the sensor captures, chosen from the Wave Lengths list. When you view a sensor, a Used on Platforms list shows the platforms that carry it.
The Platforms table lists every registered platform with its Name and Description.

On the Equipment page, click Add new Platform below the Platforms table. Fill out the platform form. Click Apply. To change a platform, click the view icon in its row, then click Edit. To remove a platform, click the remove icon in its row and confirm. A platform can't be removed while a UAV uses it.

Field Required Description Name Yes Name of the platform (example: Parrot Anafi). Description No Description of the platform. Type Yes Type of platform, chosen from the Platform Types list (example: fixed wing). Manufacturer Yes Manufacturer of the platform, chosen from the Platform Manufacturer list. Sensors At least one The registered sensors this platform can carry.

IDM hosts all published image mosaic and elevation products in the public SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog (STAC), Know-STAC, making these products available as Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs (COG). This means that all published COGs are available from standard COG API functionality. See Cloud Native Formats for why IDM uses COGs.

The most reliable way to get a COG's URL is from the product's STAC item, which lists the public URL of each of the product's files. Find the published product in the Products tab of the Site Viewer sidebar, and select Share. See Sharing a Published Product. Open the STAC link. It opens the product's STAC item, a JSON file. In the item's assets, find the file you want and copy its href: The ortho mosaic is the asset with the title Ortho. Elevation files (DSM, DTM) have the title Elevation. The COG version of each file has the type image/tiff; application=geotiff; profile=cloud-optimized, and its file name ends in .cog.tif.
documents.s: Finding the URL of a Published COG

documents.t: Every published file is at a URL with this pattern: https://osmre-uas-prod-public.s3.amazonaws.com/<site>/<project>/<mission>/<collection>/products/<product name>/<file path> For example: https://osmre-uas-prod-public.s3.amazonaws.com/justins_test_site/project/mission/flooddamagetest/products/1728194256657/ortho/odm_orthophoto.cog.tif https://osmre-uas-prod-public.s3.amazonaws.com is the public bucket of the DOI GeoPlatform installation. Each installation of IDM publishes to its own bucket. justins_test_site/project/mission/flooddamagetest is the path to the collection, starting at the site. products/1728194256657 is the product group. Each processing run or uploaded product creates its own group, so this part is different for every product. ortho/odm_orthophoto.cog.tif is the file within the product group. The file path depends on how the product was made. For example, an ortho mosaic produced by IDM processing is at ortho/odm_orthophoto.cog.tif, but elevation files and uploaded products use other paths and file names. Use the STAC item to get the exact URL rather than guessing the file path. Other installations Addresses on this page are for the DOI GeoPlatform installation of IDM. On other installations of IDM, replace https://osmre-uas-prod-public.s3.amazonaws.com with your installation's address.
Add a raster data source in QGIS and configure it to use the COG URL from the STAC item. Once added the COG is available for streaming directly from the image on s3.
documents.s: Adding a Published COG to Quantum GIS (QGIS)

documents.t: Navigate to the Report page using the navigation menu. The Report menu item is available to all users. The report page has two reports: The Processing Quality Report is a CSV file with information about each processing run in the system. It is only shown to Administrators. The Collection Report is a table with information about every collection in the system. It is shown to all users.

The Processing Quality Report bar at the top of the page generates a report on the processing runs in the system. This is where you can see information for each time a processing job is run. Choose a Since Date. The report includes the runs started on or after this date. It defaults to six months before today. Clear the date to include all runs. Push the Generate button. The report is downloaded as report.csv. The report lists the most recent runs first, up to 10,000 runs. It has these columns: Column Description collectionName Name of the collection that was processed. processedImageCount Number of images used in the run. processedImageSizeMb Total size of those images, in megabytes. taskMessage The latest message of the processing task. processingStatus The status of the processing task, such as Complete, Processing, or Failed. runDate The date the run started (YYYY-MM-DD). pocName The point of contact name of the collection. organizationName The organization of the collection's site. s3Path Where the collection is stored. uavSerial Serial number of the collection's UAV. uavFAA FAA number of the collection's UAV. sensorName Name of the collection's sensor. sensorType Type of the collection's sensor. featureQuality The feature quality processing option. radiometricCalibration The radiometric calibration processing option. odmConfig All the processing options of the run. instanceType The type of server the run was processed on. runtime (seconds) How long the run took, in seconds. Blank if the run hasn't finished.

The Collection Report provides a report on all collections in the system, including collections that have been deleted. This is where you can see information about the sensors, platforms, data size, and other information that could be useful to understand the characteristics of each collection. View the report in the table. Click a column header to sort by it, and use the boxes under the headers to filter the rows. Use the page numbers under the table to see more rows. (optional) Export the report as a CSV file (report.csv) using the Export CSV button above the table. The export always contains every row of the report. It doesn't apply the filters or sorting from the table. Column Description Collection Name of the collection. Click it to open the collection in the Site Viewer. It isn't a link if the collection no longer exists. Collection Owner Username of the user who owns the collection. Collection Date Date the data was collected. Mission Name of the collection's mission. Project Name of the collection's project. Site Name of the collection's site. Latitude Latitude of the site, in decimal degrees. Longitude Longitude of the site, in decimal degrees. Bureau Organization of the collection's site. Platform Name of the collection's platform. Sensor Name of the collection's sensor. FAA Id Number FAA ID number of the collection's UAV. Serial Number Serial number of the collection's UAV. RAW Images Count Number of files in the collection's raw folder. EROS Metadata Complete Whether the collection's metadata has been submitted. Video Whether the collection contains video. Storage size Total size of all the collection's files, in bytes. Number of Downloads Number of times the collection's imagery has been opened as a map layer. File downloads are not counted. Number of Products Number of products for the collection. Date of Create Date the collection was created in IDM. In the CSV export this column is named Date of Creation. Date of Delete Date the collection was deleted from IDM. Blank if it hasn't been deleted. Text columns are filtered by any part of the value, and RAW Images Count by an exact number. EROS Metadata Complete and Video are filtered by choosing True or False. The other columns can't be filtered.

The Session Event Log section of the System Configuration page allows administrators to monitor sign-ins to IDM. To open it, choose System Configuration from the navigation menu. The table lists the most recent events first, 20 per page. Use the page numbers under the table to see older events. Column Description Username The username or email address entered when signing in. For sign-ins through single sign-on, this is the user's email address. Bureau The organization the user belonged to when they signed in. It is blank for failed sign-ins. Event Date The date and time of the sign-in, in your browser's time zone. Event Type LOGIN_SUCCESS for a successful sign-in, or LOGIN_FAILURE for a failed one. Only sign-ins are recorded. Sign-outs and other actions are not logged.

Click the Export Session Log button to download the whole log. The download is a zip file, idm-session-log.zip, containing a CSV file named session-event-export.csv with one row per event and these columns: Column Description username Same as Username in the table. eventType LOGIN_SUCCESS or LOGIN_FAILURE. eventDate The date and time of the event in UTC, in ISO 8601 format (for example 2025-03-14T17:05:22.000Z). organization Same as Bureau in the table. The rows in the export are not guaranteed to be in date order. Sort the file by eventDate after opening it.

The System Information page shows which release of IDM is running. It is updated automatically with each release. To open it, choose System Info from the navigation menu. Only Administrators see this menu item, but any signed-in user can open the page directly at https://aim.geoplatform.gov/#/admin/system-info. Other installations Addresses on this page are for the DOI GeoPlatform installation of IDM. On other installations of IDM, replace https://aim.geoplatform.gov/ with your installation's address. The page shows: Software Versions: the IDM Platform Version and the Open Drone Map (ODM) version used for processing. Release Notes: a link to the IDM release notes on GitHub, which list the features and fixes in each release. Include the IDM version when you contact IDM support about a problem.

The UAV registration page allows for the registration and management of UAVs in IDM. Only Administrators can register, edit or remove UAVs. info If the sensor and/or platform doesn’t exist for the UAV you’re registering please see the Platforms and Sensors page.

Navigate to the UAV page by choosing UAV from the navigation menu. The table lists all the UAVs currently registered in the system, with their Serial Number, FAA Id Number, Description, Organization and Platform. Click the Add new UAV button. Fill out the form. All fields except Description are required. The Apply button stays disabled until they are filled in. Click Apply. info If you do not have a serial number or FAA number but must still register the UAV, enter “n/a” instead. Field Required Description Platform Yes Platform of the UAV, chosen from the registered platforms. Serial Number Yes Serial number of the UAV. FAA Number Yes FAA number of the UAV. Up to 10 characters. Description No Description of the UAV or any information that might be useful to know about this registration. Organization Yes Organization that the UAV belongs to. Start typing in the field to search for the organization, then select it from the list.
Scroll to the right of the registered UAV table and click the eye icon for the UAV you would like to edit. Click the Edit button on the UAV form. Change any values and click Apply.

Scroll to the right of the registered UAV table and click the remove icon for the UAV you would like to remove. Confirm that you want to remove the UAV. A UAV can't be removed while a collection uses it.

The full error is: The zip did not contain any files to process. Files must follow proper naming conventions and end in one of the following file extensions: jpg, jpeg, png The list of extensions in the message depends on the collection's format. For multispectral and radiometric collections, the message starts with "You selected a multispectral sensor." or "You selected a radiometric sensor." This error means that none of the files in the archive have a file type the collection accepts. Common causes are: The files don't match the collection's format. For example, .jpg images were uploaded to a multispectral collection, which only accepts .tif files. The archive only contains other files, such as a geo location or ground control point file, but the matching Upload includes… option wasn't checked. Check the file types in your archive against the supported file formats for the collection's format. See the file requirements for uploads.
documents.s: What does the error “The zip did not contain any files to process” mean and how can I fix it?

documents.t: All error messages for processing tasks that are accessible from IDM are found by expanding the processing task on the Workflow Tasks page. See Troubleshooting Processing Errors for what each error means and how to fix it. In cases where the log output from Open Drone Map (ODM) is able to be captured the full ODM log will be available in the processing task by pushing the “View ODM Run Information” button.
documents.s: My upload appears to be processing indefinitely. How can I find out if there are any error messages?

documents.t: There is no way to terminate a running processing task. If a step stops reporting progress, IDM fails it with the message "The task timed out (was processing for too long with no updates)." This happens after 1 day without updates for ODM processing, 3 days for storing ODM results, and 7 days for most other steps. See Timeouts and Interrupted Jobs. If your task still shows as processing after that, please contact IDM support to report your issue.
documents.s: I started processing a dataset a couple weeks ago and it shows that it is still processing. How can I terminate it or restart it?

documents.t: If the UAV you are searching for is not appearing in the search drop down the aircraft may not be registered yet. All UAVs must be registered in IDM before becoming available in the system. Please contact IDM support to register the UAV.
documents.s: The FAA ID field isn’t auto-populating with my aircraft when I begin typing in the values. How can I get IDM to recognize my aircraft?

documents.t: Sensors and platforms options are registered with IDM by an IDM administrator (see Platforms and Sensors). Please contact IDM support to request either be registered or changed.
documents.s: I can’t find my camera or platform when creating a collection. How can I get them added to IDM?

documents.t: Only required fields must be filled out. Many of the required fields are automated based on the UAV, sensor, and platform set on the collection while all others are highlighted in red. Other metadata fields are encouraged to be filled out when accurate information is known. See the collection fields.
documents.s: When creating a new collection, do I need to enter information into all of the fields or just certain ones?

documents.t: If your orthomosaic is a coarser resolution than the original it is likely because the processing settings are set to a coarser resolution than the raw data. When configuring a processing task, find the “Orthophoto and DEM Resolution (cm)” option under “Advanced Settings” in the processing options modal. Alter the resolution settings to match the resolution of the raw data. See Advanced Settings.
documents.s: The orthomosaic created by IDM lacks the detail of my original images. Why is this and how can I improve my orthomosaics?

documents.t: Warnings are indication of the system notifying you that the information may be useful for you to know but that the information is not critical. Warnings can generally be ignored but if you have questions please contact IDM support.
documents.s: Many of my uploads show warnings next to “Store” in Workflow Tasks. Should I be concerned or is there something I can do to fix this?

documents.t: In general the imagery processing task that uses Open Drone Map (ODM) may run out of memory when the raw collection is very large, the individual raw images are large, the images are challenging for ODM to stitch together, and/or the processing quality is set high. Adjusting the advanced settings before running the processing task may be useful in these situations. Try adjusting the “Generated feature quality” option and evaluate the resulting product. If adjusting the advanced settings does not work for your needs please contact IDM support to request evaluation of your situation.
documents.s: My collection failed to process with the message “ODM ran out of memory during processing.” What can I do to avoid this issue?

documents.t: Field Workers are the primary users of IDM. Their primary tasks are to upload data, process data into products, share products, and create metadata. These guides provide instructions on how to complete different tasks and workflows in the application. New to IDM? Start with Getting Started and the Data Hierarchy.

Organize your data. Create a site if one doesn't exist, then create a collection along with any new projects and missions. Upload raw data. Upload still imagery, multispectral imagery, video, or LiDAR to the collection. Monitor progress. Track uploads and processing jobs on the Workflow Tasks page. Create products. Generate products from your raw data or upload products created with other tools. Share your data. Publish products to the public, share raw images with image sets, or download files.

Organizing Data: Sites, Projects, Missions, Collections, Private Collections Uploading Data: Overview, Still Imagery, Multispectral Imagery, Video, LiDAR Monitoring: Workflow Tasks, Troubleshooting Processing Errors Working With Products: Overview, Generating Products, Geologger Files, Ground Control Points, Uploading Products, Viewing Products Sharing and Downloading: Publishing Products, Image Sets, Downloading Files
There are multiple places that files can be downloaded depending on what you’re viewing in IDM and what needs to be downloaded.
Open a collection with the raw tab selected. Right click on a raw image and select Download image.

The Download All button at the bottom of the collection modal downloads the files of the tab that is currently selected. Open a collection with the raw tab selected. Click on the Download All button at the bottom of the modal. The raw images of the collection are downloaded as a single zip file. For LiDAR collections, the zip file contains the raw point cloud files.

The supporting data tab lists the files that were uploaded with the raw images but are not images, such as a geo.txt file. Open a collection and click on the supporting data tab. Click the Download button next to the file you want. To download all supporting data files as a single zip file, click the Download All button at the bottom of the modal while the supporting data tab is selected.

The products tab of a collection displays the names of the products as hyperlinks to allow downloading individual files. Open a collection and click on the products tab. Click on the name of any product in any product group.

If a product row has a report, it can be downloaded from that row's Actions menu. Open a collection and click on the products tab. Click the Actions button on the product row. Click Download report. The Download report option only appears when a report exists for that product.

Product files can be downloaded from a collection. The download includes files that can be used in other software packages outside of IDM if more specific processing and analysis is needed. Open a collection and click on the products tab. Click on the Download All button at the bottom of the modal. info The Download All feature downloads the products from the primary product group only. The products are downloaded as a single zip file. Within the zip file, the products keep their subfolders (for example ortho, dem and ptcloud), so files with the same name, such as report.pdf, do not overwrite each other.
documents.s: Downloading All Product Files From The Primary Product Group

documents.t: The product creation process creates the products displayed in the product groups as well as files used in the product creation process. This includes the raster products, log files, and some vector files. Most of these files are not needed but they can be helpful in some situations (e.g. reading log files). Open a collection and click on the products tab. Click on the Download All Generated Data button at the bottom of the modal. The Download All Generated Data button only appears when Open Drone Map produced an all.zip file when it processed the collection. It downloads the all.zip file of the primary product group.
documents.s: Downloading Product Files and All Processing Files

documents.t: Image sets are groupings of raw images from the raw tab of a collection that are created to share sets of raw images. They make it easier to highlight selections of raw images that show something of interest. Some example uses are to share a couple raw images that have issues or highlight something in the field that stands out in the imagery.

Image sets are created from the raw tab of a collection. The Add to image set... option is only available for still imagery and LiDAR collections. It is not available for video collections. Open a collection with the raw tab selected. Right click on a raw image and select Add to image set.... Choose where to add the image: To create a new image set, clear the Use existing image set checkbox and enter a name in New image set name. To add the image to an image set that already exists in this collection, select the Use existing image set checkbox and choose the set from Select image set. If the collection already has image sets, Use existing image set is selected by default. Click Submit. Image set names may contain only letters, numbers and underscores. Spaces and special characters such as <, >, -, +, =, !, @, #, $, %, ^, &, *, ?, /, \ and apostrophes are not allowed. note An image is added to the set only if IDM can read GPS coordinates from the image's EXIF data. Images without GPS coordinates are not added.
Existing image sets can be viewed and managed from the image-sets tab of a collection.
documents.s: View and Manage Image Sets in a Collection

documents.t: Open a collection and click on the image-sets tab. Find the image set you would like to delete and click Delete Set.
Open a collection and click on the image-sets tab. Find the image set you would like to remove an image from. Click the Actions button to display the remove option. Click Remove from set.
documents.s: Remove an Image from an Image Set

documents.t: Image sets can be viewed on the map and shared from the Image Sets tab of the Site Viewer sidebar. The Image Sets tab appears after you select a location in the hierarchy, or a site, project or mission. It lists the image sets of all collections below the selected item.
documents.s: View and Share Image Sets from the Site Viewer Sidebar

documents.t: Drill into a hierarchy and click the Image Sets tab on the sidebar to display existing image sets. Each image set card shows: The image set name. A breadcrumb of the site, project, mission and collection that the image set belongs to. An Images dropdown listing the images in the set. Select an image to show its thumbnail, then click the thumbnail to open a preview of the image.

Drill into a hierarchy and click the Image Sets tab on the sidebar to display existing image sets. Click the View Centroids button on one of the image sets. Centroids will appear as turquoise points. Click on one or more centroid points to display the specific raw image in a popup.
documents.s: Displaying the Location of Image Sets on the Map

documents.t: Image sets can be shared with other logged in IDM users by URL. Drill into a hierarchy and click the Image Sets tab on the sidebar to display existing image sets. Click on the Copy URL to clipboard button to copy a link to that specific image set. The link has the form https://<IDM server>/#/site/viewer/set/<image set id>. Share the link. Opening it shows the Site Viewer with the image set's mission selected and the image set displayed on the map. info Image sets belong to their collection and follow the collection's access rules. If the collection is private, only the collection's owner and invited collaborators can see its image sets or open a link to them. Image sets in public collections can be opened by any logged in IDM user.

A collection is where the primary data is organized and operations on that data are made. Raw data is uploaded to a collection and products are generated from it. See Data Hierarchy for how collections fit with sites, projects, and missions.

From the Site Viewer, select a Site you want to add a Collection to. Click the Create Collection button at the bottom of the sidebar. It's available at the site, project, or mission level of the hierarchy. Select an existing project from the drop down – or – click Add to create a new project. Click the Next button. If you started from a project or mission, it's already selected. Select an existing mission from the drop down – or – click Add to create a new mission. Click the Next button to open the form for creating the collection. Fill out the form to create a new collection. The Next button stays disabled until the required fields are filled in. Click Next to see the summary page, then click Create. The collection and any projects or missions that were added in this process are created, and the new collection opens.

Field Description Required Collection The name of the collection. Yes Collection Date The date the collection is relevant for. Typically this is the day the data was collected in the field. If this collection period spans multiple days this should be the first day (see collection end date). Yes Collection End Date The last day of a collection period when a collection spans multiple days. If left blank, it's set to the Collection Date. Has PII Concern Indicate if the data in the collection has any Personal Identifying Information (PII). When this option is checked the collection is marked as private and prevented from being published, and the Make Collection Private option is hidden. Make Collection Private Set the collection as being private. A private collection is only visible to its owner, collaborators the owner invites by email, and system administrators. See Private Collections. No products can be published from private collections to ensure that all data from a private collection remains private. Point of Contact Point of Contact: Name Name of the person who should be contacted if there are questions of the collection. Point of Contact: Email Email of the person who should be contacted if there are questions of the collection. Collection Collection: EXIF Included A flag for indicating if there is metadata included in the EXIF headers of the data. Collection: North Bound Collection: South Bound Collection: East Bound Collection: West Bound Collection: Acquisition Date Start Date the acquisition started. Collection: Acquisition Date End Date the acquisition ended. Collection: Flying Height (ft) Height of the UAV during the acquisition flight. Collection: # of flights Number of flights taken to complete the acquisition. Collection: Percent Endlap Percent of endlap for the acquisition. Collection: Percent Sidelap Percent of sidelap for the acquisition. Collection: Area Covered (acres) Total area (in acres) covered for the acquisition. Collection: Weather conditions Weather conditions during the acquisition. Platform Platform: UAV The UAV used for acquisition. Choose Serial Number or FAA Number, then search for the UAV and select it. Yes Sensor Sensor: Name The sensor used for acquisition. Shown after a UAV is selected, and lists only the sensors of that UAV. Yes Collection Format Format of the data collected from the sensor. Shown after a sensor is selected, and lists only the formats the sensor allows (shown as Allowed Collection Formats). Yes info Don’t see the platform or sensor you used? Contact a system admin to add it for you before adding metadata for this collection. See Platforms and Sensors and UAV Registration.

Uploaded data can be accessed and managed from the collection modal. You can find a collection by navigating the hierarchy in the Data or Products tabs of the Site Viewer sidebar, or with the View Collection button of a workflow task. Selecting a collection will open the collection modal. Feature Description “raw” contains all raw images uploaded in the collection. Here, images can be viewed and excluded from processing. Click an image to preview it. Right-click an image to open a menu with Download image, Exclude image from processing (or Include image in processing for an excluded image) and Add to image set.... Excluded images are shown dimmed. For collections with a video Collection Format, the “raw” tab lists the uploaded videos instead of images. Click a video to play it. Excluded: “raw” is the only tab of the collection modal where you can process imagery into products, with the Process button. This runs ODM processing on the raw images that aren't excluded and creates a product from the outputs. See Generating Products. This process can be monitored on the Workflow Tasks page. The “supporting data” tab lists the other files uploaded with the raw data, such as a geo location file (geo.txt). Each file has a Download button, and geo.txt also has a Reupload button. The “products” tab displays the collection's product groups. Processing creates a product group named after the Product name you enter, and the Create product group button creates an empty group for uploading products made with other tools. Each group is shown by its name and has three sections: - Ptcloud contains point cloud files. ODM processing creates a .laz point cloud. - DEM contains elevation files. ODM processing creates a DSM and a DTM, each as a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (.cog.tif). - Ortho contains image mosaic files. ODM processing creates an ortho mosaic as a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (.cog.tif) and as a PNG. ODM processing also adds its processing report (report.pdf) to each section it creates. See Generating Products. NOTE: All product assets can be either automatically created by IDM data processing or manually uploaded. The “video” tab only appears for older collections that were created without a Collection Format. It lists the videos uploaded to the collection. Click a video to play it. Collections with a video Collection Format show their videos in the “raw” tab instead. The “Edit Metadata” button enables the ability to edit metadata for the collection The Download All button downloads a zip of the files on the tab you're on only: the raw images on the “raw” tab, the files on the “supporting data” tab, or the primary product group's files on the “products” tab. The “Download All Generated Data” button downloads all outputs from automatic Open Drone Map (ODM) processing. It's only shown after the collection has been processed. See Downloading Files. The “image-sets” tab lists the image sets created from the raw images of the collection. The “Access Management” button is available on private collections for inviting and removing collaborators. The share icon at the top right of the collection modal, on the same line as the collection's name, copies a link to the collection to your clipboard. Other IDM users who open the link go straight to the collection, as long as they have access to it.

There can be one or more missions within a project. A mission defines a tactical field operation to collect data in a specific area, for a specific purpose, and within a specific time range. info Projects and missions are created as part of the Create Collection form. The new mission will not be created until you successfully create a new collection using the same multi-step form you’re using to create this mission.

From the sidebar of the Site Viewer, select a site. Navigate into a project and click the Create Collection button at the bottom of the sidebar. The modal for creating and managing data organization hierarchies will appear with the project section of the modal loaded by default. Select the project you want to add the mission to and click Next. When on the section for selecting an existing mission or adding a new one, click the Add button. This will expand the options for creating a mission. Fill out the fields for the new mission. Click Next to move to the next steps in the process for creating a collection. Continue with the steps to create a collection.

Field Description Required Mission Set the name of the mission. Yes Contracting Office Set the name of the office that is managing the contract for this mission. Vendor Set the name of the vendor who is collecting the data for this mission.

A private collection is hidden from other IDM users. Only these users can see it: the collection owner collaborators the owner has invited system administrators Administrators can see private collections, but they can't view, download, publish or delete the collection's products unless the owner invites them as collaborators. info Once private: The collection owner can invite other individual IDM users to access the collection No products can be published from private collections to ensure that all data from a private collection remains private. A collection that already has published products can't be made private. Unpublish its products first. Checking Has PII concern on a collection makes it private automatically.
Follow the steps to Collections if one doesn’t exist already. Select the “Make collection private” option. Press submit to save the changes.

Once a collection is private, the owner of that collection can grant access to other IDM users by email. Collaborators can use the collection like the owner, with these exceptions. Collaborators can't: invite or remove collaborators delete the collection change whether the collection is private lock or unlock its products Only the collection owner sees the “Access Management” button. Administrators can't manage collaborators on another user's collection. Log in as the collection owner. Navigate to the private collection. Click on the “Access Management” button at the bottom left of the collection modal. Once pressed, the modal for adding collaborators will appear. Enter an email for the user who will be granted access to the private collection. Click the “Grant Access” button.
documents.s: Inviting Collaborators to a Private Collection

documents.t: Log in as the collection owner. Navigate to the private collection. Click on the “Access Management” button at the bottom left of the collection modal. Once pressed, the modal for managing collaborators will appear. Any existing collaborators will display with an option to “Remove Access”. Press the “Remove Access” button for any user whose access must be removed.
