documents.t: There can be one or more projects within a site. A project defines the operational project that all work is conducted for. info Projects and missions are created as part of the Create Collection form. The new project will not be created until you successfully create a new collection using the same multi-step form you’re using to create this project.

From the sidebar of the Site Viewer, select a site. Click the Create Collection button at the bottom of the sidebar. The modal for creating and managing data organization hierarchies will appear. When on the section for selecting an existing project or adding a new one, click the Add button. This will expand the options for creating a project. Fill out the fields for the new project. Click Next to move to the next steps in the process for creating a collection. Continue with the steps to create a collection.

Field Description Required Project Set the name of the project. Yes Short Name Set the short name of the project. A short name is a shortened version of the project name. Yes Restricted Set the project as restricted. Sunset Date Set the date for when the project is expected to be complete and/or the data is at end of life. This field is only for metadata purposes and no automated action is taken to modify or archive the data based on this date. Project Type Select the type of project. The options are: - Terrain - Imagery - Hydrography - Vegetation - Ecosystems - Forest Management - Fire & Aviation - Weather & Climate - Transportation - Recreation - Administrative Boundaries - Facilities & Infrastructure - Lands & Realty - Other
A site is the top most level of the data hierarchy and includes the location of where the data is collected.
Select the “Add new site” button on the bottom of the sidebar of the IDM Sites page. Fill out the new site form: Submit the form. Your newly created site will appear on the map and in the sidebar.

Field Description Required Name The name of the site. Yes Description A description of the site. Make Private Set the site as private so that only you (the site's owner) and system administrators can see it. Privacy isn't shared by organization; other users in your organization can't see a private site. Organization Set the organization that you work for. NOTE: if you are a cooperator with a federal agency please select that agency. Yes Site Location Each site requires a location. To set a location you can: 1. Enter longitude and latitude coordinates in fields provided 2. Click on the map to populate the longitude and latitude fields 3. Search for a specific address using the search bar Yes Site Location: Longitude Longitude for the location of the site. Yes Site Location: Latitude Latitude for the location of the site. Yes

Products are stand-alone assets made up of harmonized imagery, elevation, or LiDAR data. Products in IDM are created from one of two methods. Derived from raw data in a collection using one of the processes in IDM. Manually uploaded to the products tab of a collection. These are typically created or refined using external tools but uploaded to IDM for storage. Either way, products are stored in product groups. Processing creates a product group named after the Product name you enter, and you can create a product group yourself to hold uploaded products. A collection can have several product groups, for example from processing with different settings, and one of them is the primary group. See Product Groups. Products can be managed from a collection modal and can be viewed in the Site Viewer. Generating Products from raw data, including Geologger Files and Ground Control Points Uploading Products created with external tools Viewing Products Publishing Products Downloading Files

The collection modal is where all raw images that have been uploaded to a collection (in one or multiple uploads) and the most recently processed output products are stored. All products derived using IDM functionality are configured in the collection modal or the processing workflow and built from the data in the raw tab. IDM has two kinds of processing, depending on the collection's data. They create different products and have different options: Imagery LiDAR Collection data Still imagery (RGB and thermal), multispectral imagery and video LiDAR point clouds (LAS/LAZ) Processed with Open Drone Map (ODM), which stitches overlapping images together PDAL and SilviMetric, which work directly on the point cloud Products Ortho mosaic, elevation models (DSM and DTM) and a point cloud generated from the images Cloud Optimized Point Cloud (COPC), tree canopy cover, ground surface model and terrain model rasters Options Advanced Settings, estimated processing time, geo location and ground control point files LiDAR product options only

These steps are the same for both kinds of processing. Only the options in step 3 differ. Navigate to the collection you want to create derived products for and select the raw tab if it's not selected already. OPTIONAL and not available for video: Exclude any raw images you want to exclude from the derived products. Right-click an image and select Exclude image from processing. Excluded images are shown dimmed; to include one again, right-click it and select Include image in processing. By default all images in raw will be included in image processing unless you choose to exclude them. Click the Process button to open the processing options modal. The Process button is only shown on the raw tab, and it's disabled while a process is running. It's also disabled until the raw tab has at least two images, or at least one file for LiDAR and video collections. The modal shows different options for each kind of collection: Imagery collections (still, thermal, multispectral and video): select one or more product types (Ptcloud, DEM, Ortho), and optionally review the Advanced Settings. See Processing Imagery. LiDAR collections: select one or more LiDAR products. See Processing LiDAR. Enter a Product name. It's required, and can only contain letters, numbers, periods and underscores (no spaces or special characters). Click the Submit button. It's disabled until you enter a product name and select at least one product type. When the processing options modal closes you’ll see a message indicating the job is running with a link to the processing job. The status of the processing job will be tracked on the Workflow Tasks page and successful results from the task will be available on the products tab of the collection modal and the Site Viewer. See Viewing Products. info If the job fails, see Troubleshooting Processing Errors for imagery and LiDAR processing errors.

The products a processing job creates are stored together in a product group, named after the Product name you enter. Product groups let a collection keep the results of several processing runs side by side, for example to compare different settings. They're listed on the products tab of the collection modal. New name, new group. Processing with a new Product name creates a new product group. For imagery collections, the new group becomes the collection's primary group, which is the one downloaded by Download All. Existing name, same group. If the collection already has a product group with that name, the new outputs are added to that group instead. LiDAR rasters get their own groups. For LiDAR collections, the COPC point cloud goes in the group with your Product name, and each raster you select creates its own group named after it (for example, myproduct_terrain_model). See LiDAR Products. You can also create a product group yourself, without processing, with the Create product group button on the collection's products tab. Use it to store products made with other tools, such as an ortho mosaic created in another application. See Uploading Products, which also explains how to make a different group primary and how to delete groups.

Still imagery, thermal imagery, multispectral imagery and video are processed with Open Drone Map (ODM). ODM finds matching features in overlapping images and stitches them together into products. For video, IDM first extracts still frames from the video, and then processes them the same way.
documents.s: Processing Imagery (Still, Thermal, Multispectral and Video)

documents.t: Select one or more of these product types in the processing options modal: Product type Files created Ptcloud A georeferenced point cloud (odm_georeferenced_model.laz), generated from the images. DEM A DSM (dsm.cog.tif) and a DTM (dtm.cog.tif), as Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs, plus a hillshade of the DSM. Ortho An ortho mosaic as a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (odm_orthophoto.cog.tif) and as a PNG (odm_orthophoto.png). The .cog.tif files are Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs, a cloud native format that lets the map, GIS software and published links read just the part of the file they need. The ODM processing report (report.pdf) is added to each product type you select. The full set of ODM outputs is kept as well, and can be downloaded with the Download All Generated Data button in the collection modal.

For imagery collections, the processing options modal shows an Estimated processing time at the top once you change a product type or setting. The estimate is based on earlier processing jobs with a similar amount of raw data and similar settings, and the modal shows how many of those jobs it used ("Based on N other similar jobs"). If there are no similar jobs, the estimate is Unknown.

Geo location and ground control point files are selected when you upload raw data, not when you process it. If a collection has a stored geo location file (geo.txt) or ground control point file (gcp_list.txt), IDM uses it automatically when processing. See Geologger Files and Ground Control Points. If the collection's sensor needs a geo location file and none has been uploaded, the processing modal shows "Your sensor requires an uploaded geo location file" and you can't submit the job.

When configuring a processing job to create products for an imagery collection there are Advanced Settings options that can be used to further refine the processing job. The Advanced Settings section is always shown in the processing options modal, below the product types. Only the settings that apply to the product types you select are shown, so select the product types first. The Shown when column below lists when each setting appears. Default Values​ If the collection has been processed before, the processing options modal starts with the settings of the most recent processing job, including the product types that were selected. Only the Product name starts empty. Otherwise, the modal starts with no product types selected and the defaults in the Default column below. If the collection's sensor is marked as High Resolution (see Platforms and Sensors), the resolution defaults to 2 cm and the point cloud quality to HIGH instead. Advanced Settings Fields​ Field Description Shown when Default Open Drone Map Docs Orthophoto and DEM Resolution (cm) Set the resolution for both orthophoto and elevation outputs. Orthophoto and DSM/DTM resolution in cm / pixel. Note that this value is capped by a ground sampling distance (GSD) estimate. Ortho or DEM is selected. 5 (2 for high resolution sensors) orthophoto-resolution and dem-resolution. Matcher Neighbors Perform image matching with the nearest images based on GPS exif data. Set to 0 to match by triangulation. Ortho or DEM is selected. 0 matcher-neighbors. Minimum number of features to extract per image Minimum number of features to extract per image. More features can be useful for finding more matches between images, potentially allowing the reconstruction of areas with little overlap or insufficient features. More features also slow down processing. Ortho or DEM is selected. 10000 min-num-features. Generated point cloud quality Set point cloud quality. Higher quality generates better, denser point clouds, but requires more memory and takes longer. Each step up in quality increases processing time roughly by a factor of 4x. Options: ULTRA, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, LOWEST. Ptcloud is selected. MEDIUM (HIGH for high resolution sensors) pc-quality. Generated feature quality Set feature extraction quality. Higher quality generates better features, but requires more memory and takes longer. Options: ULTRA, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, LOWEST. Ortho is selected. HIGH feature-quality. Radiometric calibration Set the radiometric calibration to perform on images. When processing multispectral and thermal images you should set this option to obtain reflectance/temperature values (otherwise you will get digital number values). Options: - NONE: no calibration. - CAMERA: applies black level, vignetting, row gradient gain/exposure compensation (if appropriate EXIF tags are found) and computes absolute temperature values. - CAMERA+SUN (experimental): applies all the corrections of CAMERA, plus compensates for spectral radiance registered via a downwelling light sensor (DLS) taking in consideration the angle of the sun. The collection has a radiometric or multispectral Collection Format (or no Collection Format). CAMERA for radiometric and multispectral collections, otherwise NONE radiometric-calibration. Video Resolution The maximum output resolution of extracted video frames in pixels. The collection has a video Collection Format (or no Collection Format) and Ortho is selected. Blank, which uses 4000 video-resolution. Video Limit Maximum number of frames to extract from video files for processing. Set to 0 for no limit. The collection has a video Collection Format (or no Collection Format) and Ortho is selected. Blank, which uses 500 video-limit. info The advanced settings are Open Drone Map settings, which is part of IDM's internal processing engine.

LiDAR data is already a point cloud, so it isn't processed with ODM. Instead, IDM uses PDAL (the Point Data Abstraction Library) and SilviMetric to work directly on the uploaded LAS/LAZ point cloud, converting it to a cloud optimized format and creating rasters from it. LiDAR processing doesn't use the imagery product types (Ptcloud, DEM, Ortho), the Advanced Settings, the estimated processing time, or geo location and ground control point files.

For LiDAR collections, the processing options modal lists these products. None are selected by default. Option Description Generate COPC Converts the uploaded LAS/LAZ point cloud to a Cloud Optimized Point Cloud (pointcloud.copc.laz), a cloud native format, in the product. The raw tab must contain a single LAS/LAZ file. Generate Tree canopy cover Creates a tree canopy cover raster. Generate ground surface model Creates a ground surface model raster. Generate terrain model Creates a terrain model raster. Each raster option creates its own product group, named after your Product name with the raster type added (for example, myproduct_terrain_model). The rasters are made from the COPC point cloud. If you don't select Generate COPC in the same job, a product group with the same Product name that already has a COPC point cloud must exist, otherwise the job fails.

Many sensors contain embedded georeference information in their EXIF headers which are used for aligning raw images into mosaics. If this information does not exist in the EXIF headers a geologger file can be used (e.g. RX1R2 sensors). Geo location file options only appear when the collection's sensor is registered as having a geologger. They are not available for video collections.

Add the geo location (e.g. geologger) file to the zip file that contains the other raw images being uploaded to IDM. In the upload modal, check Upload includes geo location file. Fill in the two required fields: Geo location file format: choose RX1R2 or ODM to match how your file is formatted. See File Formats. Geo location file name: the name of the geo location file inside the zip. The name is not case sensitive. Files named geo.txt or pix4d.csv are recognized automatically. Click Upload. When the upload finishes, IDM checks the geo location file against the images in the collection. An RX1R2 file is converted to the ODM format. The file is stored in the collection as geo.txt, which appears on the collection's supporting data tab. If the collection already has a geo location file, the new file replaces it. You don't need to select the file again when you process the collection into products. IDM uses the stored geo.txt automatically. warning If the sensor needs a geo location file and the collection doesn't have one, IDM will not let you process the collection. The processing modal shows "Your sensor requires an uploaded geo location file." If you check Upload includes geo location file but IDM can't find a file with that name in the zip, the upload fails.
documents.s: Including a Geo Location File with a Raw Data Upload

documents.t: A geo location file can be uploaded by itself. Do this if raw data was uploaded to a collection without the geo location file, or if the geo location file needs to be replaced. Zip the geo location file by itself. Open the collection that the geo location file must be added to. Click the Upload button on the raw tab to open the upload modal. If the collection already has a geo location file, you can also click Reupload next to geo.txt on the supporting data tab. Add your zipped geo location file to the upload modal. Check Upload includes geo location file and fill in the format and file name, as described above. Click Upload.
documents.s: Adding a Geo Location File to a Collection With Raw Data Already Uploaded

documents.t: ODM based geologger files must be in .txt format adhering to the following file specification: projection image_name geo_x geo_y [geo_z] [omega (degrees)] [phi (degrees)] [kappa (degrees)] [horz accuracy (meters)] [vert accuracy (meters)] [extras...] Example: EPSG:4326 DJI_0028.JPG -91.9942096111111 46.84252125 198.609 DJI_0032.JPG -91.9938293055556 46.8424584444444 198.609

RX1R2 (Pix4D) based geologger files can be in .txt or .csv format and must adhere to the following file specification: imagename,geo_y,geo_x,z Example: IMG_3165.JPG,46.2345612,6.5611445,539.931 IMG_3166.JPG,46.2323423,6.5623423,529.823

Ground control points are useful for correcting distortions in the data and referencing the data to known coordinate systems. A Ground Control Point (GCP) is a position measurement made on the ground, typically using a high precision GPS. (Toffanin 2019) warning A minimum of 5 GCPs are required for adjusting the model. Each GCP needs to be clearly visible and have coordinates on at least 3 photos. For improved accuracy, use 5 to 10 GCPs that are evenly spread across the project area.

Ground control point files can't be used with video collections. Add the ground control point file to the zip file that contains the other raw images being uploaded to IDM. In the upload modal, check Upload includes ground control point file. Optionally, enter the Ground control point file name. The name is not case sensitive. If you leave it blank, IDM looks for gcp_list.txt. Click Upload. IDM recognizes a file named gcp_list.txt even if you don't check the box. A file with any other name is only used if you check the box and enter its name. When the upload finishes, IDM checks the file against the GCP File Format and the images in the collection. The file is stored in the collection as gcp_list.txt. If you checked the box but IDM can't find the file in the zip, the upload fails. You don't need to select the file again when you process the collection into products. IDM uses the stored gcp_list.txt automatically.
documents.s: Using a Ground Control Point File

documents.t: IDM checks the GCP file when it is uploaded. A file that does not follow these rules is rejected. The file must be a text file with a .txt extension. The first line must be exactly EPSG:4326. Coordinates must be WGS84 longitude and latitude in decimal degrees. Other projections, such as UTM or PROJ strings, are not accepted. Convert your GCP coordinates to EPSG:4326 before uploading. Each following line describes one GCP as seen in one image. Separate values with spaces or tabs, and do not include blank lines. Each line must contain at least these six values, in this order: geo_x: longitude, between -180 and 180 geo_y: latitude, between -90 and 90 geo_z: elevation im_x: pixel column of the GCP in the image im_y: pixel row of the GCP in the image image_name: the name of an image in the collection. It must match the image file name exactly, including upper and lower case. The first five values must be numbers. Do not use "NaN" for an unknown elevation; use 0.0 instead. Keep at least 7 decimal places in longitude and latitude. 0.0000001 degrees is about 1 cm on the ground, so rounding off digits reduces accuracy. An optional 7th column typically contains the label of the GCP. Any further columns are ignored. EPSG:4326 geo_x geo_y geo_z im_x im_y image_name [gcp_name] [extra1] [extra2] ... Example: EPSG:4326 -122.4062503 48.0400297 5 3044 2622 IMG_0525.jpg -122.4075806 48.0398503 5 4193 1552 IMG_0585.jpg -122.4092505 48.0396502 5 1606 2763 IMG_0690.jpg

Products created or refined using external tools can be uploaded to the products tab of a collection for storage. Products can also be uploaded to a project or mission without a collection, when you have products but no raw data to store in IDM.

Products in a collection are organized into product groups. Each group can hold one ortho, one DSM, one DTM and one point cloud, plus a report for each. There are two ways to create a product group: By processing. Processing a collection creates a product group named after the Product name you enter. If a group with that name already exists, the outputs are added to it. Manually. Click Create product group on the collection's products tab and enter a Product name. The group starts empty, and you fill it by uploading products, as described in Upload a Product. If a group with that name already exists, IDM uses that group instead of creating a new one. One product group in each collection is the primary group. The primary group is the one downloaded by the collection's Download All button. A new product group, whether created by processing imagery or with Create product group, becomes the primary group. To make a different group primary, click Make Primary on it. To delete a group, click Delete Group on it. The primary group can't be deleted directly; make another group primary first.

Navigate to the products tab of the collection modal. If you want the products in a new product group, click Create product group, enter a Product name, and click Submit. The name can only contain letters, numbers, periods and underscores. The new group becomes the primary group. Click the Actions button on the right of the row for the type of product you want to upload, and select the upload option: Ortho: Upload DEM: Upload DSM or Upload DTM. A product group can hold both a DSM and a DTM. Ptcloud: Upload An upload option is only shown while that slot is empty. To replace a product, first select Remove (or Remove All) from the same menu. Select the file to upload, fill out the form, and click Upload.
Product File types Ortho tif, tiff, png DEM (DSM or DTM) tif, tiff Point cloud las, laz Each product can also be uploaded inside a .zip or .tar.gz file.

Field Shown for Description Process upload Ortho Select whether you want IDM to generate the supporting files needed to view and stream your data or (if un-checked) to simply store the file as uploaded. If checked, IDM converts the file to a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) and a PNG preview image (thumbnail). If unchecked, the file is still uploaded and attached to the product, but it won't have a preview and won't be viewable on IDM's map. Un-check this option if the file is already in the format you want to store it in and you don't want IDM to create derivatives for additional IDM functionality beyond storage. NOTE: Uploaded ortho and elevation products are kept in their original format while an additional COG is created to support cloud native functionality in IDM and for publishing. See Cloud Native Formats. Ortho Correction Model Ortho The elevation model the ortho was corrected (orthorectified) with: DSM, DTM or Unknown. Enable Potree viewer for point cloud Point cloud If checked, IDM builds a tiled version of the point cloud (Potree format). This is required for the point cloud to be viewable in the web-based Potree viewer. If unchecked, the file is stored but won't render in that viewer. Point Cloud EPSG Number Point cloud The EPSG code of the point cloud's coordinate system. Point Cloud Projection Name Point cloud The name of the point cloud's projection. Description All A description of the product. Processing Software All Enter the software used to create the product being uploaded (ex: Pix4D). DSM and DTM uploads are always processed: IDM converts the file to a COG and generates a hillshade image from it, which is used to visualize it on the map.
Each product row's Actions menu also has Upload report (or Reupload report) for attaching a PDF report to that product, and Download report once a report exists.

If you have products but no raw data to store in IDM, you can upload them directly to a project or mission. IDM creates a standalone product group for them, with the same metadata as a collection. In the Site Viewer, navigate to the project or mission you want to add the products to. Click the Upload Products button at the bottom of the sidebar. The button isn't shown at the site level. The Upload to [project or mission name] form opens. Fill it out: Product group name: a name for the product group. Collection Date (required) and Collection End Date: when the data was collected. Optional metadata: Short Name (up to 8 characters), Sunset Date, Project Type, Contracting Office and Vendor (up to 50 characters each). The UAV, sensor and Collection Format (all required), and other collection metadata. These are the same fields as when creating a collection. Click Create. The new product group opens. Upload each product from the actions button for its type, as described in Upload a Product (steps 3 and 4). Standalone product groups are listed in the Products tab of the Site Viewer sidebar along with collection products. See Viewing Products.
Products can be viewed from the products tab of a collection or from the Products tab of the Site Viewer sidebar.

You can view and download output products on the products tab of the collection modal. The tab lists each product group in the collection, with a table of its files: Type, Name, Processing Software, Date, File Size and Description. Click a file name to download it. Product groups are created by processing the collection, with each run's Product name as the group's name, or manually with the Create product group button to hold uploaded products. The newest group becomes the primary group. If you would like to recreate the products using a different set of images or settings, process the imagery again with a new Product name; earlier product groups are kept until you delete them.

You can also view products in the Products tab of the Site Viewer sidebar. The Products tab will show all product groups that exist at or below the level of the hierarchy you are drilled into. For example, if you are on the project level of the hierarchy you will see all products at that level. If you navigate down a level to a specific mission the products will be filtered to just the products that exist for that mission. Use Order available products at the top of the tab to sort the list. If a collection has more than one product group, use its Versions list to choose which group to show. Clicking on the preview thumbnail of a product will bring up a larger preview to view more detail. Each product has the following actions. An action is disabled or hidden when it doesn't apply, for example Aerial when the product has no ortho. Action Description Aerial Maps the image mosaic of the product on the map and zooms to the extent of the image mosaic. Hillshade Maps the elevation hillshade of the product on the map and zooms to the extent of the hillshade. 3D Opens a new browser tab with a 3D (Potree) viewer containing the point cloud for the product group. Get Info Opens a detail modal with the raw image information and a link to the collection. See Product Details. Lock / Unlock Only shown to Administrators. Locks the product so that it can't be deleted, published or unpublished until it is unlocked. See Locked Products. Delete Brings up a modal that asks you to confirm that you want to delete the product, and removes the selected product if you select “Delete”. Only the collection's owner and Administrators can delete products. Not shown for locked or published products. Publish / Unpublish Publishes the product to the public. Once a product is published this option will change to “Unpublish” and you may select this to make the product no longer available to the public. Not shown for locked products. See Publishing Products. Share Only shown for published products. Opens the public links for the product. See Sharing a Published Product. Aerial and Hillshade stream the layer from the product's Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF, and 3D streams the point cloud, so only the area you're viewing is downloaded. See Cloud Native Formats.
documents.s: Viewing Products in the Site Viewer

documents.t: A locked product can't be deleted, published or unpublished. Administrators can lock and unlock products from the Products tab. Products in a collection marked as having a PII concern are locked automatically, so they can't be published.

Selecting “Get Info” will open a detail modal with the following: Thumbnail of the produced output Collection information including: Pilot Name Date the Collection was created Date the data was created in the field Sensor Information Platform information UAV information All Raw Images used to create the produced output Select the Collection Details button to access the collection directly. This is where you will be able to manage raw images. This button isn't shown for products uploaded without a collection. Select the Download ODM Files button to download a zip file of all output Open Drone Map produced for the collection. This button is only shown when that file exists.

Products can be shared publicly by publishing a specific product. The publish functionality registers the product on the public IDM Know-STAC and makes a variety of methods for accessing the data available to anyone outside of IDM. When you publish a product, IDM: copies the product's files and preview images to a public cloud storage bucket creates a public STAC item describing the product registers the product in Know-STAC, where anyone can find it Unpublishing removes the public copies and the Know-STAC entry. Access Types to a Published Product Map tile services (TileJSON) Direct cloud native access (Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF). See Public Image Services. Public IDM Know-STAC

Find the product in the Products tab of the Site Viewer sidebar. See Viewing Products. Select Publish on the product. Once a product is published this option will change to Unpublish. Select it to make the product no longer available to the public. info Products can't be published from private collections or from collections marked as having a PII concern. Products in a PII collection are locked, and locked products can't be published or unpublished. A published product can't be deleted; unpublish it first. A collection with published products can't be made private.

Find the published product in the Products tab of the Site Viewer sidebar. Select Share on the product. A dialog opens with the product's public links: STAC: the URL of the product's public STAC item. It describes the product and links to its files. Services: map tile service (TileJSON) links for the product's ortho and elevation layers, for use in web maps and GIS tools. Copy the link you need and share it.

Know-STAC (Knowledge-Enabled STAC) is a semantic layer and storage application for making STAC searches interoperable across agencies and domains. STAC (Spatio Temporal Asset Catalog) is a standard for describing and organizing cloud native data on the cloud. IDM ortho mosaics and elevation rasters are stored as Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs, a cloud native format, and are registered in Know-STAC when published. This means that products published in IDM are more: findable because that data is part of a standardized STAC specification accessible because the data a Know-STAC item points to are in cloud native formats shareable because the data is accessible by web URLs The Know-STAC browser is a web application for searching Know-STAC. See the Know-STAC documentation for more information.
This page lists the errors IDM reports while uploading and processing data, what causes them, and how to fix them. Errors are grouped by the stage of the job they happen in.

Errors are shown on the Workflow Tasks page, in the step of the processing job where they happened: Status and Message. When a step fails, its status changes to Failed (or Error) and its Message explains why. Show Messages. Some errors are listed with the Show Messages button instead, often along with warnings and other information. A message that ends with "View messages for more information" or "Check the messages for more information" means the details are in that list. Complete With Messages. A step that finished but recorded messages shows the status Complete With Messages. Check the messages: some of them, such as skipped files, may mean part of your data wasn't used. Some messages include text that comes directly from the processing tools. If your message isn't on this page, or the fix doesn't work, contact IDM support and include the full message.

Some errors don't have a specific cause you can fix, and the suggested fix is to try the upload or processing again. In those cases: warning Try only once more. If it fails a second time, contact IDM support instead of trying again. Repeated attempts are unlikely to work, use processing resources, and can make the problem harder to diagnose.

These errors happen while IDM checks the files in an uploaded .zip or .tar.gz file. See the file requirements. Message Cause Fix The zip did not contain any files to process. Files must follow proper naming conventions and end in one of the following file extensions: … None of the files in the archive have a file type the collection accepts. For multispectral and radiometric collections, the message starts with "You selected a multispectral sensor." or "You selected a radiometric sensor." Check the file types against the supported file formats for the collection's format. The uploaded file did not pass validation. Check the messages for more information. One or more files failed a check. Open Show Messages to see which files and why. The file [name] is of an unsupported format and will be ignored. The following formats are supported: … A file in the archive has a file type the collection doesn't accept. The file is skipped and the rest of the upload continues. No action needed if the file wasn't meant to be uploaded. Otherwise, check the collection's format. The filename [name] contains special characters which will be replaced with an underscore. A file name contains characters other than letters, numbers, periods and underscores. The file is renamed and uploaded. No action needed. Rename files before uploading to keep their original names. The filename [name] conflicts with another name in the uploaded archive. … This will result in missing files. Two files end up with the same name, because they were in different folders or because of replaced characters. Only the first one is kept. Give every file a unique name and upload the missing files again. The file [name] is not a valid image file An image can't be read. It may be damaged or not really an image. Remove or re-export the image and upload again. The system encountered an error while reading your zip file. Your zip file may be corrupt, or it may have gotten corrupt during upload. The archive can't be opened. Create the zip file again and upload it again. The zip file contains more than a single point cloud file. A Lidar collection can only have one raw point cloud. A LiDAR upload contains more than one LAS/LAZ file. Upload one point cloud per collection. See LiDAR. The zip file contains a new point cloud file with a different name than an existing point cloud file. A Lidar collection can only have one raw point cloud. The collection already has a point cloud with a different name. Use a new collection, or give the file the same name as the existing one to replace it. Invalid Product Name [name]. No spaces or special characters … are allowed. The product name contains spaces or special characters. Use only letters, numbers, periods and underscores. An error occurred while uploading the imagery to S3. … The upload couldn't be completed. The rest of the message gives the reason. Look up the rest of the message on this page. If it isn't listed, contact support.

These errors happen when IDM checks a geo location file or ground control point file during upload, or before processing. The upload fails with one of these messages, and each problem in the file is listed under Show Messages. Message Cause Fix Geo location file did not match the expected file format. View messages for more information. The geo location file has errors. Fix each line listed under Show Messages and upload the file again. See Geologger Files. Ground control point file did not match the expected file format. View messages for more information. The ground control point file has errors. Fix each line listed under Show Messages and upload the file again. See GCP File Format. Could not find a geo location file with name [name]. Upload includes geo location file was checked, but no file with that name is in the archive. Check the file name, or uncheck the option. Could not find the specified ground control point file [name] inside the uploaded archive. Upload includes ground control point file was checked, but no file with that name is in the archive. Check the file name, or uncheck the option. Geo-location file is invalid and cannot be sent to ODM. Upload a new geolocation file and try processing again. View messages for more information. Processing found problems in the collection's stored geo location file. Fix the problems listed under Show Messages, upload the file again, and process again. The problems listed under Show Messages include: Message Fix First line must be 'EPSG:4326' Make the first line of the file exactly EPSG:4326, and use longitude and latitude in decimal degrees. Line [n] must contain at least three values. / Expected at least 4 values on line [n]. / Line [n] must contain at least six values. Add the missing values on that line. The number needed depends on the file format. Line [n] contains a non-numeric longitude. / …latitude. / …value. Fix the value on that line. Check for text, empty values or "NaN". Line [n] contains a longitude which is out of bounds. Longitude must be between -180 and 180. / …latitude… between -90 and 90. Check that the coordinates are in decimal degrees and that longitude and latitude aren't swapped. The geo location file did not include a reference to [image] (an image in your collection). … / Image [name] exists in the collection but is not referenced in the geo-location file. Add a line for that image to the geo location file. Every image in the collection needs a location. Line [n] references an image which does not exist. Image names must match exactly and are case sensitive. Fix the image name in the ground control point file so it matches an image in the collection exactly.

documents.t: These errors happen while Open Drone Map (ODM) processes still, thermal, multispectral or video imagery. See Processing Imagery. When ODM reports more than one known problem, the message is "Errors were discovered in ODM output. See messages for more information." and each problem is listed under Show Messages. Message Cause Fix ODM ran out of memory during processing. Please contact your technical support. You can also try turning down the quality settings and re-processing. The processing server ran out of memory. This is more likely with many images, large images, or high quality settings. Lower Generated feature quality, Generated point cloud quality or the resolution in the Advanced Settings, and process again. If that doesn't work, contact support. ODM failed to produce a reconstruction from the image matches. Check that the images have enough overlap, that there are enough recognizable features and that the images are in focus. ODM couldn't match the images to each other. Check the image overlap and focus. Exclude blurry images, or images of the sky or ground, and process again. Couldn't find enough usable images. … Fewer than two usable images. Check that the raw tab has at least two images and that they aren't all excluded. Could not connect to the odm server. Please contact your server administrator. IDM couldn't reach the processing server. Wait a while, then try once more. If it fails again, contact support. The job encountered an unspecified error. The processing server returned an error without details. Try once more. If it fails again, contact support. ODM returned an unexpected response status [status]. … The processing server returned a status IDM doesn't recognize. Contact support. ODM did not return any results. (There was a problem unzipping ODM's results zip file) Processing finished, but its results couldn't be read. Process once more. If it fails again, contact support. The collection can not be processed because its product is locked. The collection's product is locked. Ask an administrator to unlock the product. Job was canceled. The job was canceled. The status is Canceled rather than Failed. Process again if needed.

These errors are specific to multispectral imagery. See Multispectral Imagery for the naming and panel requirements. Message Fix Unable to find image panel. This may effect image color quality. Did you include a panel with naming convention IMG_0000_*.tif? Include the calibration panel images, named IMG_0000_*.tif. Alignment image not found. Did you include an alignment image with naming convention IMG_0001_*.tif? Include an alignment image set named IMG_0001_*.tif. Image [name] does not match the naming convention. … Rename the images to IMG_[four numbers]_[band number].tif. Image alignment has failed. … Remove bad images (for example, images of the inside of the case or entirely black images), check the panel images, or choose a different alignment image. Make sure the collection is from a single flight. Your upload includes images with naming convention IMG_0000_*.tif, however those images do not appear to be of a panel. … Make sure IMG_0000_*.tif is of the calibration panel, and that there are no other panel images in the upload.

These errors happen while processing LiDAR data. See Processing LiDAR. Message Cause Fix Lidar processing encountered errors. View messages for more information. One or more steps failed. Open Show Messages to see the details. Expected a single laz file, but there were [n] The raw tab has more than one point cloud file. Keep only one LAS/LAZ file in the collection. Error: Could not determine SRS (Spatial Reference System) for supplied pointcloud. / Error: Could not determine CRS (Coordinate Reference System) for supplied pointcloud. The point cloud file doesn't say which coordinate system it uses. Add the coordinate system to the LAS/LAZ file's header, and upload it again. Error: Could not determine bounds for supplied pointcloud. The point cloud's extent couldn't be read. The file may be empty or damaged. Check the file in another tool, and upload it again. No point cloud files to be processed. You selected raster products without Generate COPC, and there's no product with the same Product name that has a COPC point cloud. The status is Complete, but no rasters were created. Process again with Generate COPC selected, or use the Product name of an existing product that has a COPC.

These errors happen while IDM creates the files for a product, after processing or when you upload a product. Most are listed under Show Messages, and the step may still finish with some files missing. Message Cause Fix ODM did not produce an expected file [file]. Processing didn't create one of the expected outputs, for example because the product type wasn't selected or ODM couldn't create it. Check whether the product you needed was created. If not, process once more. If it's still missing, contact support. Problem occurred generating cog file. Cog generation failed for [file]. (or a similar message about the overview file or copying the file) IDM couldn't create the Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF for a file. Check that the uploaded file is a valid GeoTIFF, then upload or process once more. If it fails again, contact support. Problem occurred generating gdal transform. PNG file did not exist. / …Hillshade file did not exist. / …TIF file did not exist. IDM couldn't create the preview image or hillshade. Check that the file is a valid GeoTIFF, then upload or process once more. If it fails again, contact support. Unable to determine the .tif(f) file and the .tif(f).aux.xml file in the archive. A product uploaded as an archive doesn't contain one .tif file and its matching .tif.aux.xml file. Put the .tif and its .aux.xml file in the archive, or upload the .tif by itself. Problem occurred running Potree Converter. IDM couldn't create the files for the 3D point cloud viewer. Check that the point cloud file is valid, then upload or process once more. If it fails again, contact support. Uploaded file ends with cog extension, but did not pass cog validation. A file named .cog.tif isn't actually a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF. IDM processes it as a regular GeoTIFF instead. No action needed. An error was encountered while processing the imagery. Something bad happened A known issue in this release of IDM. It happens when you upload an ortho as a .tif or .png file with Process upload checked. IDM usually creates the Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF and preview image before this error, so the ortho may still be usable. Open the collection's products tab and check whether the ortho's .cog.tif and .png files are there. If they are, the ortho can be used. If they aren't, contact IDM support. Error while uploading file … / An error was encountered while processing the imagery. … A file couldn't be stored or processed. The rest of the message gives the reason. Upload once more. If it fails again, contact support with the full message. Unexpected error invoking [tool] … One of IDM's processing tools failed. The rest of the message comes from the tool. Contact support with the full message. Messages about cleaning up data from ODM or sending email can be ignored. They don't affect your data.

Message Cause Fix The task timed out (was processing for too long with no updates). Contact your technical support. A step stopped reporting progress. IDM fails a step after 1 day without updates for ODM processing and for uploads that are finishing, after 3 days for storing ODM results and processing uploaded orthos, and after 7 days for other steps. Contact support before processing again. The server was shut down while the task was running. The IDM server restarted during the step. Start the upload or processing once more. If it fails again, contact support. A step with status Failed and no message is usually an upload that was canceled.

The Raw directory (RAW tab) of a Collection is where unprocessed or minimally processed data from a flight is stored. Uploading to the Raw directory ensures that your data is stored on the government cloud in a compliant manner and makes the data available for generating derived products. Each type of data has its own requirements and steps: Still Imagery (RGB and thermal) Multispectral Imagery Video LiDAR Before uploading, create a collection to upload the data to if one doesn't exist already.
Data type File extensions Still images (RGB, thermal as RGB) jpg, jpeg, png Multispectral images tif, tiff Radiometric (thermal) images tif, tiff Video mp4 LiDAR las, laz

All files uploaded to the raw tab of a collection must be compressed into a .zip or .tar.gz file. IDM checks each file in the archive when the upload finishes. The results are shown on the upload's task on the Workflow Tasks page. Folders: files inside folders in the archive are uploaded, but the folders are not kept. All files are placed directly in the raw tab. File names: only letters, numbers, periods (.) and underscores (_) are kept. Any other character, including spaces and hyphens (-), is replaced with an underscore. For example, IMG 001-a.jpg is stored as IMG_001_a.jpg. Duplicate names: if two files end up with the same name, because they were in different folders or because of replaced characters, only the first one is kept. The others are skipped with an error message. Unsupported file types: files that don't match the collection's format are skipped with an error message. See Supported File Formats. If no files in the archive are supported, the whole upload fails. info To avoid skipped files, give every file a unique name that uses only letters, numbers, periods and underscores. For example, IMG_001.jpg is a valid file name.

Automated metadata​ Metadata for sensors, platforms, and UAVs are configured for the system by administrators which enables automation of parts of the metadata for each collection because the UAV, sensor, and platform must be assigned to the Collection. It’s strongly encouraged to fill out as much of the remaining metadata as possible to ensure data is compliant with storage and retention requirements. Additional (optional) metadata​ Sites, projects, missions, and collections all have optional metadata that should be filled out to ensure data is compliant with storage and retention requirements.

Data uploads go through two basic steps. The data is uploaded to the IDM server. The data is processed to un-zip files, audit for issues, and automatically store data in compliant locations with the correct metadata assigned. The post processing step (step 2 above) can take more time than the initial upload (step 1 above). You can monitor the progress of the upload in the Processing Jobs section of the Workflow Tasks page. info If the upload fails, see Upload Errors in Troubleshooting Processing Errors.

Now that your data has been successfully uploaded you can manage that data from the collection modal. You can access the collection modal from several locations in the application: By navigating through the hierarchy in the Site Viewer to the Site → Project → Mission → Collection. By selecting the “View Collection” button on the workflow task associated with the collection you uploaded data to. From the collection you can generate products from the raw data.

Multispectral imagery can be uploaded to the raw directory of collections for storage as well as for further processing into derived products.
MicaSense RedEdge-MX and Altum Sentera 6X DJI Phantom 4 Multispectral DJI Mavic 3 Multispectral

All files uploaded must be compressed into a .zip or .tar.gz file. See the file requirements. The uploaded zip is recommended to be of a single flight. Image naming convention must be IMG_[four numbers]_[band number].tif. There must be five bands if the data is from a RedEdge sensor or six bands if the data is from Altum. The images with name IMG_0000_*.tif (set of 5 or 6 bands) must be of the panel. This image is optional but highly recommended for proper calibration. There must be no other panel images anywhere else in the uploaded zip. The images with name IMG_0001_*.tif (set of 5 or 6 bands) must exist, and is used to calibrate the alignment for the rest of the image collection. It is for this reason it is assumed that the uploaded zip is of a single flight. It is up to you to pick a good image to use for alignment, ideally one with lots of reference point objects such as cars, buildings or large chasms. If the camera experiences a shock event (ex. banging into a tree) the calibration may become invalid and images after the shock event may be misaligned as a result. Some flights may not have the optimal images for calibration for reasons like the recording starts while the UAV is on the ground (no birds eye view yet). In these cases the raw images must be manually adjusted to meet this requirement. Take the time to look through your image collection and weed out any bad images, i.e. pictures of the camera inside the case, or pictures which are entirely black, etc. This will ensure the best chance of processing success for your flight. info It is best to zip all images you want to upload into a single .zip file rather than doing multiple uploads. The application was designed to handle very large .zip files (containing a lot of images) even in a low bandwidth environment.

The Workflow Tasks page is the central location for monitoring data uploads and processing, and for actions required on data that has been uploaded. Open it by choosing Workflow Tasks from the navigation menu in the upper right of the application. The page has two main sections: Tasks and Processing Jobs.

The Tasks section appears only when there are tasks that need your attention. It provides a list of items that the user needs to take action on in order to complete the item’s workflow; like filling out metadata for example. Each item in the list has a description of the issue and buttons to associated actions. Feature Description The issue description contains details about the problem with the associated collection in [ ]. The Site / Project / Mission / Collection is also listed for reference. Select View Collection to open the collection modal associated with the task. Select the Add Metadata button to open a form to complete the metadata for the collection. Completing the metadata will complete the task and remove it from this list.

The Processing Jobs section provides a list with the status of all uploads and processing for your user. The name of the job in the list is the collection name, and the Site / Project / Mission / Collection is also listed for reference. Select View Collection to open the collection modal associated with the job. For product uploads that are not attached to a collection, the job is named after the product and has a View Product button instead. View Product opens the details of the product. The list has two tabs: All shows every job. This tab is selected when the page opens. Action Required shows only jobs with a status of Failed. Each processing job has a status indicator: Color Status Orange (blinking) Processing Green Complete Blue Complete with messages (warnings or errors that did not stop the job) Red Failed

Clicking on the name of a processing job will expand it to show the status of each step. There are three types of steps: Upload: monitors the process for uploading data to the IDM server and the post-processing steps needed to properly audit and store all data. Process: monitors processing jobs that create derived products (image mosaics, elevation, and point clouds) from raw data previously uploaded. Store: monitors the process for moving derived products from the processing environment to permanent storage. Each step shows its Current status and can be expanded to show more detail and provide information for troubleshooting and data management. For each task in the step, the details include the Status, the creation and last update dates, and a Message. Upload steps also show the Sensor. A task that completed but has messages shows the status Complete With Messages. While Open Drone Map is processing a collection, the Process step can also show a Runtime Estimate. IDM estimates the processing time from previous processing runs with a similar amount of raw data and similar settings. The estimate is shown only when IDM can calculate one. Longer estimates also show a more exact time in parentheses, for example "3 hours (2h 54m)".

In the case that there are warnings or errors you can troubleshoot the issue by selecting the Show Messages button. Select Hide Messages to close the list. info For what each error means and how to fix it, see Troubleshooting Processing Errors. If the job has failed there will be a message explaining the issue: When a step has finished, more buttons may be available to view details and address any issues: Show Detailed Log Output shows the log from processing. View ODM Run Information opens the details of the Open Drone Map run, including its full log. View Run Configuration shows the settings used for a LiDAR processing run. See Troubleshooting Processing Errors for a list of errors and their fixes, and the Frequently Asked Questions for common issues.

Most people already have accounts in that staging instance but if you have problems logging in please make sure you have an account in this staging environment by attempting to login or creating a new account if needed in this environment: https://idp.int.identitysandbox.gov/ tip Your account must be added to IDM by an administrator before you can sign in. See Accounts if you are an administrator.
IDM stores the products it creates in cloud native formats. This page explains what that means, why IDM uses them, and where you'll find them in IDM.

Imagery, elevation and LiDAR files are often several gigabytes each. With traditional file formats, you have to download the whole file before you can look at any part of it. Cloud native formats organize a file so that software can read just the part it needs, directly from cloud storage over the internet. To show a small area of an ortho mosaic at a given zoom level, a map only reads the few pieces of the file that cover that area. The rest of the file is never downloaded. The files are still ordinary, standard files. Desktop tools such as QGIS and ArcGIS can open them like any other GeoTIFF or LAZ file.

IDM was built for teams that work in remote locations with limited, unreliable internet, and that need to share large datasets across an organization. Cloud native formats support that directly: Work in low bandwidth. You can view products on the map, zoom in and pan around without downloading the full files. Only the data on your screen is transferred. One copy serves every use. The same file is used for map display, download, analysis and public sharing. IDM doesn't have to build and store separate map tiles or preview copies, so there's less to keep in sync and less storage to pay for. Easy sharing. Once a product is published, anyone can stream it straight from its public URL into their own GIS software, without asking for a copy or downloading the whole file. See Public Image Services. Open standards. The formats are open, widely supported standards, so data stored in IDM isn't tied to IDM and stays usable by other tools and agencies. Findable data. Published products are described with STAC, a standard catalog format, so they can be searched and found alongside data from other systems. See Know-STAC.

Format Used for Created when Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG), files ending in .cog.tif Ortho mosaics and elevation models (DSM, DTM) IDM processes imagery, or you upload an ortho or DEM Cloud Optimized Point Cloud (COPC), files ending in .copc.laz LiDAR point clouds You process a LiDAR collection with Generate COPC Potree point cloud tiles The 3D point cloud viewer IDM processes imagery into a point cloud, or you upload a point cloud with Enable Potree viewer for point cloud SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog (STAC) Descriptions of published products, with links to their COG files You publish a product When you upload an ortho or DEM, IDM keeps your original file and creates a COG alongside it. If you uncheck Process upload, the original is stored as-is, without a COG, and won't display on IDM's map.

Where How cloud native formats are used Site Viewer map Aerial and Hillshade draw ortho and elevation layers by streaming tiles from the product's COG as you pan and zoom. 3D streams the point cloud into the Potree viewer. Products tab of a collection Lists the .cog.tif and .copc.laz files with the rest of each product's files, ready to download. Publishing Copies the product's files, including its COGs, to public cloud storage, and creates a STAC item that links to them. Public Image Services Explains how to stream published COGs into QGIS and other GIS software. Know-STAC The public catalog where published products' STAC items can be searched. LiDAR processing Tree canopy cover, ground surface model and terrain model rasters are created from the COPC point cloud.

documents.t: In IDM data is organized in a hierarchy. The standard hierarchy is: Site Project Mission accessible_support Collection raw video products This standard way of organizing data provides consistency to how data is stored, how data is classified, and how data is described (metadata) within the hierarchy. Level Description Site A site is the top most level of the data hierarchy and includes the location of where the data is collected. Project There can be one or more projects within a site. A project defines the operational project that all work is conducted for. Mission There can be one or more missions within a project. A mission defines a tactical field operation to collect data in a specific area, for a specific purpose, and within a specific time range. accessible_support There is only one accessible_support folder per mission. Accessible_support is a storage folder for supporting data (e.g. documents) that are relevant to the mission. Collection There can be one or more collections within a mission. A collection is where the primary data is organized and operations on that data are made. Collection: raw The raw directory of a collection stores the data in its most raw form directly after collection. See the supported file formats. Collection: video The video directory stores videos that are manually uploaded to a collection's video folder. Collection: products The products directory stores the products generated from raw data or manually uploaded to the products directory directly. Administrators can also configure custom hierarchies that can be used to browse sites in the Site Viewer.
Create a site Create a collection, including any new projects and missions

Support for IDM is provided at two levels. Start with your organization's help page, and contact the IDM help desk only when your organization's support can't resolve the issue. tip If an upload or processing job failed, check Troubleshooting Processing Errors first. It explains the error messages IDM shows and how to fix many of them.

Each organization can publish its own help page in IDM, with its help desk contacts, support hours, request templates, documentation and training resources. This should be the first place you go for support. Click Need some help? in the header at the top of any IDM page. The help page opens in a new browser tab. The page shows the help content for your organization. If your organization doesn't have its own help page, the page for a higher-level organization that it belongs to is shown. Follow your organization's instructions to request support. The help page also links to this documentation and to the GeoPlatform documentation. If the help page is empty or doesn't cover your issue, ask your IDM administrator. Administrators set up the organization help pages; see Help Pages.

TerraFrame operates a help desk for IDM. Use it for general IDM support when your organization's support isn't able to resolve the issue. To open a ticket, email support@terraframe.com. To help the help desk resolve your issue quickly, include: what you were trying to do, and the steps you took any error messages, and screenshots if possible the names of the site, project, mission and collection involved, if any for processing or upload problems, the job's details from the Workflow Tasks page

The Site Viewer is your landing page and provides access to key functionality. Its sidebar and map are your primary tools for uploading and exploring data. To return to the Site Viewer from another page, choose Site Viewer from the navigation menu in the upper right of the application.

The highest level of the data hierarchy and first page of the Site Viewer is the IDM Sites page. Feature Description The sidebar lists all sites contained in the map extent and filters based on the area of the map. Selecting (clicking on) a site in the sidebar will take you to the Projects level of the hierarchy and will highlight the site on the map. The sidebar shows 50 sites at a time. When there are more, use the page controls at the bottom of the sidebar to move between pages. If your site does not exist, select the “Add new site” button to create a new site. Use the search bar for location based search and to search the hierarchy for existing data. Use the Hierarchy dropdown to filter the Sites in the sidebar by either the default IDM Hierarchy or any other custom hierarchies that have been integrated with the system. Use the advanced filter to narrow down what’s shown in the sidebar. View different basemaps by hovering over the layers icon in the upper right corner of the map and selecting Outdoors, Satellite, Streets or OSM. Select the Search GeoPlatform button (magnifying glass) in the upper left corner of the map to search for published products in the area shown on the map, and add them to the map. See Searching Know-STAC from IDM. Select the Mapped Images button (globe) in the upper left corner of the map to see every product, image set and GeoPlatform image currently on the map. The number on the button is how many layers are on the map. For each layer you can Show or Hide it, Zoom to it, Remove it from the map, or Get Info about it. Use the zoom controls to zoom in and out on the map - this will also filter the sites based on the map extent. The latitude and longitude of the location of your cursor on the map is shown on the bottom right of the map. Select the navigation menu icon in the upper right of the application to access other pages and navigate away from the Site Viewer, including the Workflow Tasks page where you monitor uploads and processing.

The sidebar is used to navigate the hierarchy to find a collection and/or products. Selecting a tile from the sidebar will take you to the next level of the hierarchy. The hierarchy navigation is Site → Project → Mission → Collection and the Collection will be where all raw images and produced outputs are accessed and managed. Once you have selected a site, the sidebar has additional functionality: Feature Description Navigate to different levels of the hierarchy by clicking on the breadcrumb trail at the top of the panel. You now have the option to view Data, Products, or Image Sets. Data contains all hierarchy navigation and shows all items contained on that level of the hierarchy. Products contains all output products contained in the current level of the hierarchy. For example if you are on the Project level you will see all produced output for every project contained in the site, if you select a project you will only see produced outputs for that project. See Viewing Products. Image Sets contains the image sets in the current level of the hierarchy. See Image Sets. The Create Collection button at the bottom of the panel will open the wizard where you will be able to configure and create a Collection. Selecting the arrow in the upper right of any tile will expand the tile to reveal the next level of the hierarchy.
Products published from IDM are registered in Know-STAC, where anyone can search for and access them.
info All data on Know-STAC is publicly accessible. No credentials are needed. Know-STAC server: https://knowstac.geoprism.net/dev/

Know-STAC (Knowledge-Enabled STAC) is a semantic layer and storage application for making STAC searches interoperable across agencies and domains. The Know-STAC browser is a web application for searching Know-STAC.
The Know-STAC application is a single page web application with the primary components being the map and sidebar.

The sidebar is where most of the functionality is found. It contains two tabs that toggle between the search and results modes. Search Tab​ Search mode is where searches are configured and contains all the search parameters available. Results Tab​ Results mode displays the results of a search. The search results are a STAC collection with the STAC items contained within it. When a search is run the results mode is automatically enabled but can be manually toggled back and forth.
The map is where search result locations are shown. When Know-STAC items contain locations the points are displayed.

All searching functionality can be accessed from the sidebar when the search tab is selected. The following search parameters are available from the search tab: Search Parameter Description IDM Integration Relevance Restrict results to extent Restricts the results of a search to the bounds of the map when clicking the search button. Date range (start & end) Restricts search results to data within the specified date range. This filter uses the collection date field from IDM. Agency Restricts search results to the agency the data is sourced from. This filter uses the organization field from IDM. Collection Restricts search results to the name of the collection the data comes from. This filter uses the collection name from IDM. Description Restricts search results by the description of the data. This filter uses the collection description from IDM. Platform Restricts search results to the name of the platform used to create the data. This filter uses the platform name of the collection's UAV from IDM. Project Restricts search results to the name of the project the data was collected for. This filter uses the project name from IDM. Sensor Restricts search results to the name of the sensor used to create the data. This filter uses the sensor name field from IDM. Site Restricts search results to data within the specified site. This filter uses the site name from IDM. Title Restricts search results by the title of the STAC item. IDM uses the collection name as the title. UAV FAA Number Restricts search results to data from UAVs with the given FAA number. This filter uses the FAA Number of the collection's UAV from IDM. UAV Serial Number Restricts search results to data from UAVs with the given serial number. This filter uses the Serial Number of the collection's UAV from IDM.

The sidebar has two modes, search and results, as indicated by the two tabs at the top. Both modes can be toggled manually. When a search is run the results tab is automatically activated to show the results of the search.
Check the Restrict results to extent box in the sidebar. Push the Search button at the bottom of the sidebar.
When a search is run the results tab is enabled automatically and the resulting STAC collection, metadata, and STAC items are shown in both the sidebar and the map.

The STAC collection metadata is at the top of the search results. It contains the spatial extent and the temporal extent. Metadata Property Description Spatial Extent The spatial extent of all the results of the search (cumulative STAC items). Temporal Extent The min and max time range of all the data returned.

The items section includes a list of all the STAC items in the collection. Item Properties​ Know-STAC item properties are all the properties that are included on a STAC item and searchable within Know-STAC. They can be viewed by clicking the view details button to expand a STAC item. Property Description IDM Integration Reference Date Time The date that the data was collected. The collection's Collection Date. If it is empty, the Collection End Date is used, and if that is also empty, the date the product was last updated. Agency The organization who manages the data or that created the data. The site's organization, followed by each of its parent organizations. Collection The name of the collection. The collection name. Description A description of the data. The collection description. Platform The name of the platform used to collect the data. The platform of the collection's UAV. Project The name of the project that the data was collected for. The project name. Mission The name of the mission that the data was collected for. The mission name. Sensor The name of the sensor used to collect the data. The collection's sensor. Site The name of the site that the project is within. The site name. UAV FAA Number The FAA number of the UAV used to collect the data. The FAA Number of the collection's UAV. UAV Serial Number The serial number of the UAV used to collect the data. The Serial Number of the collection's UAV. Title The name of the STAC item. This is a standard STAC metadata property. The collection name. Operational The geographic locations the site falls within, from the top of the hierarchy down. The site's location in the custom hierarchy synchronized from GeoPrism Registry (STAC property geoplatform:operational). Empty if no custom hierarchy is synchronized or the site isn't in it. Assets The list of assets within this STAC item. An asset is an actual dataset. A STAC item can have one or more assets. See below. For products uploaded directly to a project or mission instead of a collection, Title and Collection contain the name of that project or mission. IDM adds these assets to a STAC item, depending on which files the product has: Asset Description Ortho The orthomosaic GeoTIFF. Elevation The digital elevation model (DEM) GeoTIFF. Overview A PNG image of the orthomosaic. Thumbnail A small PNG preview of the orthomosaic. Point clouds and other product files are not included as assets. Sharing an Item​ Each item has a share button that will open a new browser tab with the STAC definition as JSON.

You can also search Know-STAC without leaving IDM, and view the results on the Site Viewer map. In IDM, Know-STAC is called GeoPlatform. In the Site Viewer, pan and zoom the map to the area you want to search. Select the Search GeoPlatform button (magnifying glass) in the upper left corner of the map. The Search GeoPlatform for Products panel opens in the sidebar. Click Search map extent. The panel lists the published products within the area shown on the map. For each result: Click View Details to see its thumbnail and properties. Click View Extent to zoom the map to it. To add it to the map, open View Details, choose the image in the Asset list, and check Add to map. Check Show collection extent on map to outline the results on the map. Click Clear results to start a new search, or the back arrow to close the panel. Products you add to the map are listed in the Mapped Images panel (globe button), where you can show, hide, zoom to or remove them.
Know-STAC allows for sharing results by URL. Simply copy the URL for a search from the browser.
To add data from IDM to Know-STAC, publish the product. Unpublishing a product removes it from Know-STAC.
